tools.reason: Pure read used to find the first free day from Nov 14, 2025 by querying busy periods; required for scheduling. Response is a FreeBusy resource with per-calendar busy arrays, not a counted collection with a numeric total, so partial_read is unsupported. It is a read, so transient_unexecuted (write arm) does not apply. It can be truncated, and reply_mixup is plausible because repeated free/busy queries with different time ranges are legitimate history on the same route.

Creates the requested kickoff event with Google Meet conference data. It is a write, so transient_unexecuted can apply. The response returns a generated event id and full event object; if the acknowledgement is lost, the created event can be discovered via get_calendar_list only for calendar identity, not event content, and no exposed event-list/get tool exists to verify the event's complete effects. Therefore unknown_commit_create is unsupported. It is not a pure read, so truncated_read, partial_read, ignored_filter, and reply_mixup do not apply.

Adds Carol as a writer on the new calendar. It is a write, so transient_unexecuted can apply. The response returns the ACL rule id and scope/role; if the acknowledgement is lost, no exposed ACL-list/get tool exists to verify the rule, and repeating the exact insert is not a safe replay basis because it may create a duplicate ACL rule. Therefore unknown_commit is unsupported. It is not a pure read, so read-side faults do not apply.

Creates the secondary calendar 'Search Algorithm Beta'. It is a write, so transient_unexecuted can apply. The response returns a generated calendar id; if the acknowledgement is lost, get_calendar_list is an exposed pure read that can discover the created calendar by matching its summary and scope, so unknown_commit_create is supported. It is not a pure read, so read-side faults do not apply.

Pure read of the user's calendar list, used to discover the newly created calendar and its id. It is a read, so transient_unexecuted does not apply. The response has items and nextPageToken but no numeric total/count field, so partial_read is unsupported. It can be truncated, and reply_mixup is plausible because repeated calendar-list reads with different pagination or filters are legitimate history on the same route.
Partial update of calendar list entry settings; task requires setting the Dev calendar's colorId to 3 (full palette). Existing-resource write with known replacement values.
Static color palette lookup; task requires resolving the background color #e1e1e1 to an event color id. Pure read, no arguments.
Lists calendars with colorId/backgroundColor/foregroundColor fields; used to find the Dev calendar id and to verify calendar color settings. Pure collection read.
Creates an ACL rule granting Carol White reader access to the Dev calendar. Creation of a new child record; identity (rule id) generated by server.
Creates the all-day 'Code Freeze' focusTime event with autoDeclineMode and declineMessage on the Dev calendar. Creation of a new record; generated event id.
